overview.title: Dedicated to healthy smiles for all ages.
overview.text: Pick a treatment to see what it involves, or call and talk it through with our front desk.

services.title: Implant Dentistry
services.summary: Implants placed and restored in one office.
services.text: Our dental staff can use the latest technology in dental implants and individualized restorations to help you achieve a better smile.
services.lead: For specialized teeth replacement and complex cases, a dentist like Dr. Sea who has been specially trained in placing implants and restoring them is the one to see.

covers.title: 3D CT planning
covers.text: Before surgery, Dr. Sea uses a state-of-the-art 3D CT scan to plan the most ideal implant location, and takes a post-op scan to verify placement.

covers.title: What an implant is
covers.text: A small screw of biocompatible material such as titanium that replaces the missing tooth root and anchors the replacement crown, bridge or denture.

covers.title: Advanced teeth replacement
covers.text: A custom plan using crowns, bridges, dentures and implant-supported restorations that look, feel and function like real teeth.

covers.title: Full smile makeovers
covers.text: Health and function are restored first, then cosmetic improvements. Some people need one or two procedures, others a series.

questions.q: What is a dental implant, and how does it work?
questions.a: The dentist places a small titanium post into the jawbone to replace the missing root, and then adds a porcelain crown after the bone has grown around the metal.

questions.q: Am I a good candidate for dental implants?
questions.a: You need healthy gums and enough jawbone thickness to hold the post, but our Baytown team can do simple bone grafts first if you have bone loss.

questions.q: How long do dental implants last?
questions.a: The metal screw locks into your jaw permanently for life, but the crown on top takes a lot of wear from chewing and usually needs changing after ten years.

questions.q: How many appointments does the dental implant process take?
questions.a: The treatment takes a few months but only requires three main visits to handle your initial scans, the actual surgery, and the final crown attachment.

questions.q: Does dental implant surgery hurt?
questions.a: Local anesthesia blocks all pain while the dentist works, so you only deal with a dull ache for a few days that standard drugstore painkillers fix easily.

questions.q: How much do dental implants cost at Dynamic Dental Solutions in Baytown?
questions.a: The cost is determined by how many teeth are to be replaced. That is why our Baytown staff will provide you with a clear cost sheet and monthly financing options during your exam.

questions.q: Does insurance cover dental implants?
questions.a: Many dental policies pay for the surgical post or cover a percentage of the crown, and our front desk calls your provider directly to maximize those benefits.

services.title: Complete & Partial Dentures
services.text: We make high-quality complete and partial dentures, as well as implant-supported dentures, to help you get your oral health back in order.
services.lead: If you are missing one or several teeth, dentures are one of the most effective ways to get back your chewing ability and eat the foods you love. A denture also improves your smile's appearance and facial profile.

covers.title: Partial dentures
covers.text: A gum-colored acrylic base with acrylic or ceramic replacement teeth, anchored in place by your natural teeth, or fixed by crowns capped over the teeth on either side of the gap.

covers.title: Complete dentures
covers.text: Replacement teeth on an acrylic base for an entire upper or lower arch, placed either right after extractions or once the gums have healed.

covers.title: Implant-supported dentures
covers.text: Dental implants anchor a partial or complete denture. It is incredibly stable and requires no adhesive or cutting down of healthy teeth.

questions.q: How long does it take to get dentures?
questions.a: Several weeks from start to finish, with a few appointments along the way for adjustments. Extracting beforehand will add time.

questions.q: Will my dentures look natural?
questions.a: We match the shape and shade to your existing teeth as closely as possible. Most patients find that nobody around them notices anything different.

questions.q: What's the best way to care for dentures?
questions.a: Brush them with a soft brush and denture cleanser every day, and soak overnight. Hot water can cause the material to warp, so avoid using it. Always bring your dentures with you to dental visits.

questions.q: What are implant-supported dentures, and are they worth considering?
questions.a: Implant-supported dentures do not rest on the gums but connect directly to implants placed into the jawbone, which means no slipping will occur. Patients with solid bone density find them noticeably more comfortable than standard dentures.

questions.q: What should I do if existing dentures no longer fit right?
questions.a: Bone and gum tissue change over time and affect the fit, so the dentist will examine them and tell you whether a reline or a replacement is the better call.

questions.q: Do you accept insurance for dentures in Baytown?
questions.a: We take most PPO plans and file claims on your behalf. Cherry financing is available if you need to break the cost into payments.

services.title: Full-Mouth Reconstruction
services.summary: Complete smile restoration for complex cases.
services.text: We specialize in complete smile restoration using multiple restorative and cosmetic treatments to address complex dental concerns and improve your oral health.
services.lead: Smile makeovers happen every day at our Baytown office. A full-mouth reconstruction is a restorative procedure that goes beyond teeth replacement: Dr. Sea examines your mouth and jaw thoroughly and determines the best way to make these structures work together properly.

covers.title: Who it helps
covers.text: Severely stained or discolored teeth, several missing teeth, bite problems, old failing restorations, advanced gum disease with loose teeth, congenital mouth abnormalities and complex combination cases.

covers.title: One plan, several treatments
covers.text: Some patients only need whitening and bonding; others need gum disease treatment, tooth-colored fillings, veneers, crowns, dentures and implants.

covers.title: Function before appearance
covers.text: Damage, disease and decay are corrected first, then cosmetic improvements are made to the smile and facial profile.

covers.title: World-class dentistry
covers.text: Dr. Sea has the advanced training and experience to perform dental reconstruction, cosmetic dentistry and dental implants, and favors difficult and unusual cases.

questions.q: How long does full-mouth reconstruction take at Dynamic Dental Solutions?
questions.a: Most patients spend between six months and a full year completing their entire dental plan. The clinic splits the work into separate visits so your gums and jaw have time to heal.

questions.q: Is full-mouth reconstruction painful?
questions.a: Deep numbing blocks all sensation during your actual appointments, so you remain comfortable in the chair. Normal swelling occurs later, but regular over-the-counter medicine keeps that temporary discomfort under control.

questions.q: How much does full-mouth reconstruction cost in Baytown, TX?
questions.a: The price will depend on what specific treatments and appliances are involved. We have an entire pricing menu that will be shared with you prior to the procedure, including our financing options.

questions.q: Will my insurance cover any part of full-mouth reconstruction?
questions.a: Providers usually pay for structural repairs like root canals, extraction, or protective crowns. The front desk contacts your provider directly to apply those benefits to your bill.

questions.q: What is the difference between full-mouth reconstruction and a smile makeover?
questions.a: Reconstruction fixes the actual mechanics of your bite so you can eat without pain or difficulty. Makeovers only change how your front teeth look visually without treating the underlying disease or bone loss.

questions.q: How do I get started with full-mouth reconstruction?
questions.a: Contact the Baytown office at (281) 837-9090 to set up your initial diagnostic exam. The doctor looks at your mouth, takes digital scans, and builds your schedule from those results.

services.title: Emergency Care
services.summary: Prompt treatment for urgent dental problems.
services.text: Our team provides prompt and compassionate treatment for urgent dental issues, including severe pain and infections, so you can return to comfort quickly.
services.lead: Knowing which dental issues need emergency care can save you from visiting a dentist unnecessarily. If a tooth breaks or has completely dislodged from the socket, emergency dental care is necessary to save it.

covers.title: When to come in quickly
covers.text: A large missing piece, a tooth knocked out completely, infection, pain that radiates to the jaw, a toothache with fever, a dental abscess, or sore gums with severe pain.

covers.title: A knocked-out tooth
covers.text: Pick it up by the crown, rinse off any dirt and put it back in the socket, biting on gauze. If it will not go back, store it in milk and come straight in.

covers.title: A broken tooth
covers.text: Keep the broken pieces, rinse them in warm water and store them in milk. A cold compress helps reduce bleeding until you are seen.

covers.title: What usually is not an emergency
covers.text: A lost filling or crown that is not causing severe pain, a chipped tooth with no nerve exposed, a minor toothache, or broken retainers or braces.

covers.title: Holding a replanted tooth in place
covers.text: The socket is cleaned and the tooth is put back, held with a special wire. Over a few weeks the bone grows and makes the tooth stable again.

questions.q: I am not sure whether this is an emergency. What should I do?
questions.a: Call us on (281) 837-9090 and our dentists will guide you.

questions.q: Do you see emergency patients the same day in Baytown, TX?
questions.a: We fit most emergency patients in the same day or the next morning. Call (281) 837-9090 as soon as the pain starts so we can get you a slot.

questions.q: What dental problems actually count as emergencies?
questions.a: A knocked-out tooth, abscess, severe jaw pain with fever, or a fracture exposing the nerve all need same-day care. Minor chips and lost fillings without pain can wait for a regular visit.

questions.q: My tooth just got knocked out. What do I do before I reach your office?
questions.a: Hold the tooth by the crown, rinse it gently, and try placing it back in the socket. If that is not possible, store it in cold milk and call (281) 837-9090 immediately.

questions.q: Can you treat a dental abscess the same day?
questions.a: Yes, abscesses are prioritized at our Baytown office because infections progress quickly. If you see swelling, fever, or a bad taste around the tooth, call us.

questions.q: How do I manage the pain before my emergency appointment?
questions.a: Take an over-the-counter pain reliever as directed and hold a cold compress against your cheek. This only controls the pain temporarily and will not correct the cause of it.

questions.q: Do I need insurance for a dental emergency in Baytown?
questions.a: No, we see patients with and without insurance. We have payment options, and we discuss costs up front before anything is started.

questions.q: What does an emergency dental visit entail?
questions.a: We take care of the biggest problem first and plan return visits for the rest. You leave with a plan for what's next and how to take care of yourself at home.

services.title: Crowns and Bridges
services.summary: Caps for damaged teeth and bridges for gaps.
services.text: A crown caps a damaged or decayed tooth and a bridge replaces one that is gone, both made to match the shade of the teeth around them.
services.lead: A crown is a cover or cap put on a damaged or decayed tooth, covering the whole tooth rather than only the front surface. A bridge is used when a tooth is lost completely, supported by the healthy teeth on each side of the gap.

covers.title: When a crown or bridge is suggested
covers.text: To replace a filling when most of the tooth has been lost, when a tooth may fracture or be lost, to replace a missing tooth, to cover a dental implant, or to cover a broken or crooked tooth.

covers.title: How it is made
covers.text: The tooth is reduced in size and an impression is taken for the lab. If porcelain is used, the shade is matched to the surrounding teeth.

covers.title: A temporary in between
covers.text: A temporary crown covers the tooth until the permanent one comes back from the lab and is cemented in place.

covers.title: Making it last
covers.text: Crowns and bridges can last a lifetime with good oral hygiene. Brushing, flossing and regular visits keep the gums healthy so the restoration stays put.

questions.q: How long do crowns and bridges last?
questions.a: Most hold up for 10 to 15 years, sometimes longer. Regular cleanings and the condition of the teeth around the restoration make a real difference in how long it stays intact.

questions.q: How many visits will a crown or bridge require?
questions.a: Two visits for most patients. The first preps the tooth and takes impressions, the second fits the permanent piece. A temporary crown covers the tooth between appointments.

questions.q: What materials do you use for crowns?
questions.a: There are two main kinds: porcelain and ceramic. The dentist will make a recommendation based on the position of the tooth and whether strength or appearance is the priority.

questions.q: Can a crown be placed on a tooth that has had a root canal?
questions.a: Yes, and it is usually the recommended next step. Root canal-treated teeth lose moisture over time and crack more easily, so a crown keeps the tooth protected and functional.

questions.q: Will insurance cover a crown in Baytown?
questions.a: Most PPO plans cover part of the cost. The team submits your claim and walks you through what you owe before treatment starts.

questions.q: When would I need a crown or bridge?
questions.a: A crown is a cap that covers a damaged tooth but is still rooted in the jaw. A bridge replaces a missing tooth. Your dentist checks your X-rays and tells you which one applies to your situation.

questions.q: Does getting a crown hurt?
questions.a: The tooth is numbed before anything starts. You will feel some pressure during the procedure, and mild sensitivity for a few days after is normal.

services.title: Cosmetic Dentistry
services.summary: Veneers, bonding and tooth and gum reshaping.
services.text: Porcelain veneers, esthetic bonding, tooth and gum reshaping and whitening, from a quick smile makeover to full mouth rehabilitation.
services.lead: Your smile is one of the first things that people notice. Whether it is a quick smile makeover or full mouth rehabilitation, Dr. Sea has the training and experience to help.

covers.title: Porcelain veneers
covers.text: Very thin ceramic shells bonded to the tooth's surface. They hide severe stains and large fractures, cover gaps and change the appearance of individual teeth.

covers.title: Esthetic bonding
covers.text: An affordable, less invasive alternative to veneers. Tooth-colored composite corrects minor gaps, stains and chips, usually in one visit.

covers.title: Esthetic recontouring
covers.text: Changing the size and shape of a tooth and smoothing the enamel, usually with no anesthesia. Excess gum tissue can be reshaped for a more uniform look.

covers.title: Tooth whitening
covers.text: Professional whitening for a brighter smile in one visit, with a protective barrier over the gums and soft tissues, or safely at home with take-home trays.

questions.q: What is the difference between cosmetic dentistry and general dentistry?
questions.a: General dentistry deals with problems such as cavities and gum disease, while cosmetic dentistry is concerned only with changing the appearance of your teeth.

questions.q: Does insurance cover cosmetic dentistry?
questions.a: Most insurance companies refuse to pay for purely visual changes, but will cover part of the bill if the tooth is broken.

questions.q: How do I know which cosmetic treatment is right for me?
questions.a: You can book a simple exam at our Baytown location to show the dentist exactly what you want to fix.

questions.q: Are cosmetic dental procedures permanent?
questions.a: Veneers and bonding permanently alter your tooth surface during the process, so you must expect to update the restorations down the road.

questions.q: Will cosmetic dental work look natural?
questions.a: The dentist shapes your new restoration to match the unique shade and light reflection of the teeth right next to it.

questions.q: What is a smile makeover, and how is it planned?
questions.a: A smile makeover groups multiple cosmetic choices into one streamlined plan to handle several stained or gapped teeth at the same time.

services.title: Teeth Whitening
services.text: Our experts can help you brighten your smile by several shades with both professional in-office whitening treatments and easy-to-use take-home trays.
services.lead: With time and age the enamel picks up stains and the shade of your teeth darkens. Whitening removes those stains, either in the office or at home with trays.

covers.title: What stains teeth
covers.text: Acidic food and drink, smoking, fizzy drinks, tea and coffee, and letting oral hygiene slide.

covers.title: In-office whitening
covers.text: A protective barrier is placed over the gums and soft tissues and a bleaching gel is applied, in a single visit.

covers.title: Take-home trays
covers.text: At-home bleaching trays for patients who would rather whiten in their own time.

covers.title: Possible side effects
covers.text: Whitening can cause temporary tooth sensitivity when the peroxide reaches the dentin. The sensitivity fades after some time.

questions.q: What is the teeth whitening service offered at Dynamic Dental Solutions?
questions.a: We offer in-office whitening that can be completed in one visit or custom take-home trays for those patients who prefer to whiten on their own time.

questions.q: How many shades whiter can professional whitening get?
questions.a: It depends on your starting shade and the staining involved, but professional whitening gets results that store-bought products simply do not match.

questions.q: Is professional teeth whitening safe for enamel?
questions.a: Yes, and if you already have sensitive teeth, mention it to the dentist before treatment so accommodations can be made.

questions.q: How long do whitening results last?
questions.a: One to three years, mainly shortened by coffee, tea, wine, and tobacco.

questions.q: Does whitening work on crowns, veneers, or bonding?
questions.a: Whitening does not affect crowns, veneers, or fillings, so they may need replacement to match the new tooth shade.

questions.q: How is professional whitening different from store-bought strips?
questions.a: The whitening agent is much stronger, and custom trays distribute it evenly on every tooth. Strips tend to leave uneven results.

questions.q: How much does teeth whitening cost?
questions.a: Pricing varies by in-office and take-home options. As insurance usually does not cover whitening, call (281) 837-9090 or ask about our current specials.

services.title: Root Canal Treatment
services.summary: Saving a decayed or infected tooth.
services.text: A root canal treatment saves a decayed or infected tooth by removing the pulp and cleaning the inside of the tooth.
services.lead: Root canals are tiny passageways that branch off beneath the tooth. When the pulp inside becomes infected it causes pain, sensitivity and sometimes an abscess.

covers.title: Signs you may need one
covers.text: Severe pain while chewing, pimples on the gums, a cracked tooth, extreme sensitivity, swollen gums or a discolored tooth. X-rays confirm it.

covers.title: The procedure
covers.text: Usually one to three visits. A small hole is drilled through the top of the tooth, the diseased tissue is removed, the canals are cleaned and reshaped, then filled with an elastic material.

covers.title: Afterwards
covers.text: A temporary filling holds until a permanent seal is made with a crown. Most patients have little or no discomfort and keep a tooth that lasts almost as long as a healthy one.

covers.title: Post-treatment care
covers.text: Wait for the numbness to wear off before eating so you do not hurt your tongue or cheeks. Keep up proper brushing, flossing and follow-up checkups, and report any pain or swelling to us straight away.

questions.q: Is a root canal as painful as people think?
questions.a: The procedure feels like a filling; it's the infection that hurts, not the treatment.

questions.q: Is it better to get a root canal or just pull the tooth?
questions.a: Saving the tooth preserves your jawbone and alignment, and is usually less involved and cheaper than extraction plus a replacement.

questions.q: Am I covered by insurance for a root canal in Baytown, TX?
questions.a: Most PPO plans cover at least part of it, and we handle your claim and give you a cost estimate before we start.

questions.q: How do I know if I need a root canal?
questions.a: Indications that there may be an infection in the pulp are prolonged pain, sensitivity to hot or cold temperatures, swelling of the gums, and discolored teeth.

questions.q: How long does a root canal take?
questions.a: Most root canals wrap up in one or two appointments of about 60 to 90 minutes each.

questions.q: What happens if I skip a root canal my dentist recommended?
questions.a: The infection spreads, can become an abscess, and turns a simple fix into a serious and expensive problem.

services.title: Sedation Dentistry
services.summary: Nitrous oxide and oral conscious sedation.
services.text: Our top priority is your comfort. Anxiety is not an illness, it is a condition, and we encourage patients not to fight it but to use these options to take care of their oral health.
services.lead: We are happy to take care of you. Two kinds of sedation are offered at the Baytown office, and which one fits depends on the treatment and your medical background.

covers.title: Nitrous oxide (laughing gas)
covers.text: The safest kind of sedation, used in children and adults. Quick onset and offset, so you will not need a driver to pick you up after the appointment.

covers.title: Oral conscious sedation with triazolam
covers.text: Conscious sedation that makes you sleepy and unaware of the procedure. You will need a driver to bring you and take you home. It is the most common type used during implant surgery.

questions.q: Will I be completely unconscious during sedation dentistry?
questions.a: Most techniques keep you in a heavy, drowsy state where you remain awake and able to respond to the dental team.

questions.q: Will I need someone to drive me home after sedation?
questions.a: You must arrange for a friend or family member to drive you home and plan to rest for the afternoon if you choose oral or IV sedation.

questions.q: What sedation options are available in Baytown, TX?
questions.a: The Baytown clinic offers various sedations that can effectively deal with any level of anxiety that you may have, according to your medical background.

questions.q: Is sedation dentistry safe?
questions.a: Yes, it is entirely safe if performed by a dentist who evaluates the reactions of the patient throughout the procedure.

questions.q: Can sedation dentistry help me get more work done in fewer visits?
questions.a: Being entirely calm lets the dentist treat several conditions in just one appointment while you're sitting in their chair.

questions.q: I have had bad dental experiences in the past. Is sedation right for me?
questions.a: Past dental trauma is the main reason patients request sedation to get through their necessary cleanings and restorative appointments without fear.

questions.q: Does insurance cover sedation dentistry?
questions.a: Many dental plans pay for sedation if you undergo a complex oral surgery, such as a difficult tooth extraction.

services.title: Sleep Disorder / Anti-Snore Therapy
services.summary: Oral appliances for snoring and mild apnea.
services.text: Custom oral appliances for simple snoring and mild to moderate obstructive sleep apnea, as an alternative or an adjunct to CPAP and surgery.
services.lead: Sleep disordered breathing covers several conditions caused by airway blockage: large tonsils, a long soft palate, excessive fleshy tissue or the tongue relaxing too far. In our dental sleep practice we also see snoring caused by a small or retruded jaw.

covers.title: When an oral appliance is the answer
covers.text: Clinical trials show oral appliances are very effective for simple snoring and mild to moderate obstructive sleep apnea, and they can remove the need for surgery, medication or CPAP.

covers.title: Who they suit
covers.text: Patients who cannot handle or will not comply with CPAP, who will not consent to surgery, or who need the appliance alongside surgery or CPAP treatment.

covers.title: Working with your physician
covers.text: Dentistry is an integral part of sleep medicine. A trained sleep dentist works with physicians as a member of the sleep team.

covers.title: Recommended practice
covers.text: Oral appliance therapy is recommended by the American Academy of Sleep Medicine and the National Institutes of Health for mild to moderate obstructive sleep apnea and in all cases of CPAP intolerance.

covers.title: Signs to watch for
covers.text: Snoring, daytime sleepiness, an awakening headache, TMJ soreness on awakening, fatigue, restless or fragmented sleep and gasping, anxiety with breathlessness, and dozing when reading or sitting.

covers.title: Referral for a diagnosis
covers.text: When our office suspects a patient is having apneic episodes, they are referred to an ENT, a pulmonologist or a sleep specialist for a complete medical assessment and usually an overnight polysomnogram.

questions.q: How is a dental oral appliance different from a CPAP machine?
questions.a: While CPAP forces you to breathe via a face mask, an oral appliance is designed to fit comfortably into your mouth like a normal night guard.

questions.q: What does the process of getting an anti-snore appliance involve?
questions.a: We take digital impressions of your teeth during your first visit and then adjust the custom laboratory mouthpiece for a comfortable fit a few weeks later.

questions.q: Can a dentist actually help with snoring and sleep apnea in Baytown, TX?
questions.a: The dentists at our Baytown office make custom oral devices to move your jaw forward, keeping your airway open throughout the night to prevent any snoring whatsoever.

questions.q: How do I know if I have sleep apnea or just snore?
questions.a: Waking up gasping for air and feeling exhausted all day points directly to obstructive sleep apnea, which we diagnose by coordinating a formal sleep study with local doctors.

questions.q: How long does it take to see results from an oral sleep appliance?
questions.a: You will notice a major drop in snoring volume during the first few nights, while your daytime energy levels will improve steadily over the first month of treatment.

questions.q: Does insurance cover sleep apnea oral appliances?
questions.a: Most health insurances have provisions for covering a sizable portion of the cost of custom oral appliances after your doctor officially identifies you as having sleep apnea.

questions.q: Is the oral appliance comfortable to wear every night?
questions.a: Your jaw muscles need about a week to adjust to the new resting position, after which any initial tightness or extra saliva disappears completely.

services.title: Tooth Extraction
services.summary: Removing a tooth that cannot be saved.
services.text: Removal of a tooth that cannot be saved, including wisdom teeth, with sedation available for patients who need it.
services.lead: It is quite common for children to lose their teeth, but when an adult loses a tooth it becomes troublesome. Apart from wisdom teeth, an extraction may become necessary for several reasons, and the procedure at our Baytown office is simple and safe.

covers.title: Why a tooth is extracted
covers.text: A decayed or damaged tooth that can no longer be repaired with a filling or a crown, a crowded mouth being prepared for teeth straightening, or an infection in the pulp that root canal therapy cannot clear.

covers.title: The procedure
covers.text: A dentist or oral surgeon gives local anesthesia that numbs the area, then opens the gum and bone tissue covering the tooth and lifts it out. A blood clot forms in the socket and you bite on a gauze pad; a severe cut is closed with a few self-dissolving stitches.

covers.title: Aftercare
covers.text: Use an ice bag straight after the procedure to keep swelling down, avoid spitting forcefully for 24 hours, eat soft food, avoid smoking, keep your head elevated while sleeping and avoid drinking through a straw. Recovery takes a few days.

covers.title: When to call us afterwards
covers.text: Severe pain hours later, bleeding that will not stop, infection in the extraction area, fever and chills, vomiting, redness and swelling, or a cough, chest pain or shortness of breath.

covers.title: Filling the gap
covers.text: A gap lets the surrounding teeth shift and changes your bite, so the dentist will suggest an implant, a bridge or a denture to fill the space.

questions.q: When does a tooth actually need to be extracted?
questions.a: Extractions become inevitable when teeth are severely infected or damaged to the point where they cannot be restored with a crown or root canal.

questions.q: Does tooth extraction hurt?
questions.a: The area is numbed before anything starts, so you feel pressure but not pain, and some soreness over the next few days is normal and handled with medication.

questions.q: How long is the recovery after a tooth extraction?
questions.a: Within just three days, most patients are back on track with their eating habits as well as their normal activities, provided that they adhere to the post-treatment guidelines.

questions.q: What is dry socket, and how do I avoid it?
questions.a: Dry socket occurs when the blood clot that forms in the socket is prematurely dislodged from its place. Avoid the use of straws, smoking, and hard rinsing in the first two days following the procedure.

questions.q: Can you do emergency tooth extractions in Baytown, TX?
questions.a: Yes, call (281) 837-9090 and we will work to get you in the same day, particularly if infection is involved, since that should not be left untreated.

questions.q: Does insurance cover tooth extraction at Dynamic Dental Solutions?
questions.a: Most PPO plans cover at least part of the cost, and we verify your coverage beforehand so you know what to expect before the appointment.

questions.q: Do I need to replace a tooth after extraction?
questions.a: Leaving a gap causes neighboring teeth to shift over time and leads to bone loss in the jaw, so the dentist will discuss implant, bridge, or partial denture options at your appointment.

process.title: How we care for your smile
process.text: A great dental experience starts with trust and personal attention from the very first visit. Your appointment begins with a detailed consultation where we listen to your goals and answer all your questions, and during the exam our team uses advanced tools and imaging to check every aspect of your dental health.

steps.title: Find your dentist
steps.text: Consider your dentist as a long-term partner in keeping you healthy, because regular visits are important for maintaining your oral health.

steps.title: Professional consultation
steps.text: A consultation is a focused meeting where your dentist carefully examines your teeth and creates a plan for your personal dental goals.

steps.title: Timely treatment
steps.text: Book your recommended procedure as soon as possible to take care of any problems and follow the treatment plan discussed during your visit.

steps.title: Aftercare recovery
steps.text: Your dentist will give you clear instructions for recovery, and following them closely helps ensure long-term healing and results.

about.title: A well-rounded dental practice in Baytown, serving our community since 1982.
text: Dynamic Dental Solutions provides a wide range of exceptional dental services in Baytown, TX. We are one of the few practices in the Houston area offering implant surgery, implant restorations, implant-retained dentures, complete and partial dentures, and advanced full smile makeovers.

We are a team of uniquely gifted and talented individuals who have come together to provide an extraordinary level and array of dental services to people in exchange for our own personal fulfillment. We help those who come to us for care to claim, or reclaim, their own self-esteem by enabling them to chew and speak with comfort, and to smile with confidence.

Our approach is patient-centered, not doctor-centered. You are our honored guest. The office sits on three beautiful wooded acres in Baytown, with comfortable rooms and state-of-the-art equipment, and you are welcome to come and see it in person.

values.title: Patient-centered care
values.text: Our friendly and knowledgeable team takes care of you at every step, from the moment you book your appointment to your follow-up visits.

values.title: A focus on wellness
values.text: What we do goes beyond tooth repair. Whether you have difficulty chewing, extensive tooth damage or advanced gum disease, we have the skills and technology to bring your mouth back to optimum health.

values.title: On time and prepared
values.text: To be on time for your appointment, to be totally prepared and ready for it, and to finish everything that we start.

values.title: Comfort first
values.text: To provide all of our services with no or absolutely minimal discomfort, and to exhibit genuine concern before, during and after your treatment.

values.title: Our philosophy
values.text: Dentistry gives our team a window of opportunity to help people become all that they can be. The mouth has important emotional ties to self-confidence, self-esteem and an overall sense of well-being, so our work goes far beyond repairing teeth.

team.name: Dr. Benjamin Thomas
team.bio: Born and raised in Houston. Bachelor of Science in Biology at the University of Alabama, a Master's program in Biomedical Sciences, and a Doctorate of Dental Medicine at Western University of Health Sciences in Pomona, CA, where he was a founding member and president of the Endodontic study club. He completed a General Practice Residency at UTHealth Houston with advanced training in IV and oral conscious sedation, third molar extractions, special needs patients and bleeding disorders.

team.name: Dr. Jue Sea
team.bio: Bachelor of Science in Biochemistry from the University of Texas at Austin and a dental degree from the University of Texas Health Science Center at San Antonio. He served two years in a public health center in Potosi, Missouri, then practiced general and implant dentistry in the greater Houston area. He has completed implant preceptorship training, placed over 200 dental implants and restored over 100 cases, with extensive post-graduate training in cosmetic dentistry, pediatric dentistry, wisdom tooth extraction and endodontics.

team.name: Haley Brock
team.bio: A practicing dental hygienist since 2019, with an AAS in Dental Hygiene from Lamar Institute of Technology in Beaumont, TX, graduated summa cum laude, and CPR certified. Her volunteer work includes Bingham Head Start, an adult day care facility and Smile Generation Serve Days.

faqs.a: We accept and file claims for all PPO insurance plans. If your plan is not listed, our team will work to maximize your benefits so you get every dollar you are entitled to.

faqs.q: What if I do not have insurance?
faqs.a: We offer financing through CareCredit and Cherry, and payment plans, so dental care stays accessible.

faqs.q: What forms of payment do you take?
faqs.a: PPO insurance plans, CareCredit, Visa, MasterCard, Discover, American Express and Texas CHIP.

faqs.q: I am anxious about the dentist. What are my options?
faqs.a: Anxiety is not an illness, it is a condition. We offer nitrous oxide for adults and children, and oral conscious sedation with triazolam for longer treatment and implant surgery.

The practice sits on three beautiful wooded acres in Baytown, with comfortable rooms and state-of-the-art equipment. Call to arrange a visit before you book treatment if you would like to see it first.

faqs.q: What should I expect on my first visit?
faqs.a: We will check your teeth, take any needed X-rays, and talk about a treatment plan that fits your goals.
Yes. We welcome new patients and are open Monday to Friday to fit your schedule.

faqs.q: Can I use my HSA or FSA for dental treatments?
faqs.a: Yes, you can use an HSA or FSA for most treatments, saving on taxes while caring for your teeth.

faqs.q: Can a dentist help with snoring?
faqs.a: Yes. We provide custom oral appliances that help clear your airway for better sleep.

facts.heading: Dynamic Dental Implant Assurance Program
facts.text: Your dental implant is protected by a warranty. Our surgery success rate is greater than 95%, and Dr. Sea provides an extraordinary 5-year implant warranty. We monitor your implant annually for 5 years absolutely free, and we take a 3D image scan before and after implant placement so you have pre- and post-operation records.

facts.heading: If an implant ever fails
items: Year 1: we replace the implant absolutely free of charge, including removing the failing implant and placing a brand new implant with bone transplant and gum graft, with no charge for the second surgery
Year 2: 80% discount off our regular fee
Year 3: 70% discount off our regular fee
Year 4: 60% discount off our regular fee
Year 5: 50% discount off our regular fee
